Using the Threatline review process for EVAL-04 (not a WAT workflow task).

**Design summary:** Customers download invoice PDFs from `/invoices/{invoiceId}/download`. Invoice IDs are sequential. PDFs contain customer name, billing address, and last four digits of card. Deterministic signals flag `auth: false` and `payment: true`.

This is a textbook Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) setup: predictable sequential IDs + no stated authentication/ownership check on a sensitive document endpoint.

```json
{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Invoice download endpoint", "Invoice PDF generator"],
    "dataStores": ["Invoice records"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Customer browser to invoice service"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "payment"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Sequential invoice IDs let anyone download other customers' invoices",
      "scenario": "An attacker increments the invoiceId in /invoices/{invoiceId}/download (ids are sequential numbers) to pull PDFs belonging to other customers, exposing their name, billing address, and card digits without proving ownership.",
      "component": "Invoice download endpoint",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download. Invoice ids are sequential numbers." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.2", "V4.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone can change a number in the download link and see another customer's invoice, including their card digits.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce ownership check on invoice download",
        "given": "A customer requests /invoices/{invoiceId}/download",
        "when": "The invoiceId does not belong to the authenticated customer",
        "then": "The server returns 403/404 and does not return the PDF"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "No authentication required to download invoices",
      "scenario": "The design's deterministic signals indicate auth is not enforced (auth: false) for this payment-data feature. Without login, any unauthenticated requester could hit the download endpoint directly and retrieve invoice PDFs containing PII and partial card data.",
      "component": "Invoice download endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "{\"dataClasses\":[\"pii\",\"payment\"],\"exposure\":\"internal\",\"llmFeatures\":false,\"fileUpload\":false,\"auth\":false,\"payment\":true,\"thirdParty\":[]}" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "The download link may not require logging in at all, so anyone with a link (or a guessed number) gets the invoice.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require authenticated session for invoice download",
        "given": "A request hits /invoices/{invoiceId}/download",
        "when": "No valid authenticated customer session is present",
        "then": "The server rejects the request before any invoice data is read or rendered"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "PDF bundles PII and partial card data with no stated access control",
      "scenario": "The invoice PDF itself contains customer name, billing address, and the last four digits of the card. Combined with the enumerable endpoint, a single successful request leaks a bundle of PII and payment data that could be scraped at scale across many invoice ids.",
      "component": "Invoice PDF generator",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The PDF contains the customer name, billing address and the last four digits of the card." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.3.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "Each invoice PDF has enough personal and card info that leaking many of them at once is a real privacy and fraud risk.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Limit and audit bulk access to invoice PDFs",
        "given": "Invoice PDFs contain PII and partial payment data",
        "when": "A client requests many invoice ids in a short period",
        "then": "The system detects and blocks the enumeration pattern per customer/session, in addition to per-request authorization"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Predictable sequential invoice ids make targeted enumeration trivial",
      "scenario": "Because invoice ids are plain sequential numbers rather than random/opaque identifiers, an attacker can script a sweep from id=1 upward to harvest every customer's invoice without needing to guess or brute-force anything complex.",
      "component": "Invoice download endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Invoice ids are sequential numbers." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-1230"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because invoice numbers go 1,2,3..., an attacker can just count through them to find everyone's invoices.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Use non-sequential identifiers for invoice URLs",
        "given": "An invoice download URL is generated",
        "when": "The identifier is derived",
        "then": "The identifier is a non-sequential, non-guessable value (e.g. UUID) in addition to server-side authorization checks"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Using the Threatline Security Reviewer role for this task (not the WAT coding workflow, since this is a Jira threat-model review request).

Based on the context returned by get-review-context, here's my analysis and the threat model I'll submit for EVAL-04:

**Summary of key risks found:**
- Invoice IDs are **sequential**, and the endpoint `/invoices/{invoiceId}/download` gives no indication of an authorization check (auth signal is false) — this is a classic enumeration/IDOR risk exposing other customers' PII and partial card data.
- The PDF itself bundles PII (name, billing address) with payment data (last 4 card digits), increasing blast radius of any single leak.

```json
{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Invoice download endpoint", "PDF generator"],
    "dataStores": ["Invoice records"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Customer browser to invoice download endpoint"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "payment"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Sequential invoice IDs let attackers read other customers' invoices",
      "scenario": "An attacker with a valid session simply changes the invoiceId in /invoices/{invoiceId}/download to a neighboring number. Because invoice ids are sequential, they can iterate through them and download any customer's invoice, getting name, address and card digits for many customers with almost no effort.",
      "component": "Invoice download endpoint",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download. Invoice ids are sequential numbers." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.2", "V4.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone can guess invoice numbers and download other customers' invoices, exposing their name, address and card digits.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce per-user authorization on invoice access",
        "given": "a customer is authenticated",
        "when": "they request /invoices/{invoiceId}/download",
        "then": "the system verifies the invoice belongs to that customer before returning the PDF, and returns 403/404 otherwise, regardless of the invoiceId value guessed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "No authentication check on the invoice download endpoint",
      "scenario": "The deterministic signals for this item show auth is not present on the endpoint. If the download route doesn't require a logged-in session at all, anyone with a link or guessed URL can pull an invoice containing PII and card data without ever proving who they are.",
      "component": "Invoice download endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "/invoices/{invoiceId}/download" },
        { "quote": "The PDF contains the customer name, billing address and the last four digits of the card." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the download page doesn't check who you are, anyone who finds or guesses a link gets someone else's billing info.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require authentication before serving invoices",
        "given": "an unauthenticated request",
        "when": "it hits /invoices/{invoiceId}/download",
        "then": "the system rejects it and redirects to login instead of returning the PDF"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "PDF bundles PII with partial card data in one easily-shared file",
      "scenario": "Because the invoice PDF contains the customer's name, billing address and last four card digits together, a single leaked or forwarded PDF (email, shared drive, browser cache) exposes enough personal and payment data for social-engineering or card-testing attacks against that customer, beyond what the invoice workflow needs to show.",
      "component": "PDF generator",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The PDF contains the customer name, billing address and the last four digits of the card." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.8.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "The invoice file packs name, address and part of the card number together, so if it leaks once, an attacker gets a useful bundle of personal data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Minimize sensitive data in invoice PDFs",
        "given": "an invoice PDF is generated",
        "when": "it includes payment details",
        "then": "only the minimum needed (e.g. masked card reference) is shown and a data-minimization review confirms no unnecessary PII/payment fields are included"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No way to tell who actually downloaded a given invoice",
      "scenario": "If the endpoint doesn't tie downloads to an authenticated, authorized identity (per the auth:false signal and the predictable URL), there is no reliable record of which customer or attacker pulled a specific invoice, making it impossible to investigate a reported data leak of card/billing info.",
      "component": "Invoice download endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Without login tied to each download, you can't find out later who actually saw a given customer's invoice.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Attribute every invoice download to an authorized identity",
        "given": "a PDF is downloaded",
        "when": "the request is served",
        "then": "the authenticated customer or staff identity and the invoice id are recorded so access can be reconstructed during an investigation"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
